sentences.text:
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2 - de-facto complainant.
2.

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the entire proceedings in S.C. No.35/2022 on the file of learned II Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Ballari,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 304B, 498A read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: II Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank before the Trial Court.

4. The brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:
The marriage of accused No.1 and deceased Shravanti performed on 12.03.2020 at Suryabhavan Kalyanmantap, Anantpur Road, Ballari.
At the time of marriage, the complainant had given cash of Rs.8,00,000/- and gold ornaments weighing about 8 tholas as dowry to accused No.1.
After the marriage, the relationship of accused No.1 and deceased Shravanti was cordial for a period of three months.
Thereafter, all accused persons started to harass the wife of NC: 2024:KHC-D:9683 accused No.1 in respect of demand of dowry.
In spite of convening so many panchayats, accused No.1 and these petitioners did not mend their behaviour.

On 21.11.2021 in between 04:00 p.m. to 04:40 p.m., Shravanti committed suicide by hanging herself to the ceiling fan with the help of saree in the house of accused No.1 and accused Nos.1 to 8 abetted her to commit suicide.
The death was occurred within seven years of the marriage.
Hence, the de-facto complainant lodged complaint.
This led to registration of FIR and investigation.
Soon after the receipt of charge sheet, the committal Court took cognizance and committed the matter to the Court of Sessions.

5. Taking exception to the same, accused Nos.2 to 8 have filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., contending that they have falsely implicated in this case and no case is made out against them.
They never harassed and never abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
Hence, the counsel prayed to allow the petition.
6. Learned HCGP and counsel for de-facto complainant submit that there is sufficient material against these accused persons.

The Trial Court dismissed the discharge application NC:
2024:KHC-D:9683 filed by accused persons under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. and proceeded with framing of charge.
Hence, they prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 7. Perused the material available on record.

As per the charge sheet materials, it appears that C.W.1,
C.W.15 and C.W.16 have categorically stated under Section 101 of Cr.P.C. that soon before the death,
deceased Shravanti had informed them about alleged harassment made by accused persons and they were harassing her on account of dowry and in this regard, she committed suicide.
8. At this juncture, the petitioners have disputing the question of fact that cannot be gone into under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
Hence, there are no merits in the contention.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
9. In view of dismissal of the petition, pending I.As. if any, stands disposed off accordingly.
